checklist.name: pyogenic sterile arthritis or other arthritis

quotes.text: typically with the appearance of sterile pyogenic arthritis first
There were 54 (85.7%) patients who developed arthritis
Osteoarticular manifestations were described in 72% (31/43) of cases

checklist.why: Defining PAPA feature and usually the first sign; also common in PAMI.

checklist.name: pyoderma gangrenosum

quotes.text: followed by cutaneous symptoms, including pyoderma gangrenosum
26 (41.3%) with PG

checklist.why: Defining cutaneous feature of PAPA; also reported in PAMI.

checklist.name: acne (including cystic acne or acne conglobata)

quotes.text: including pyoderma gangrenosum and severe acne
34 (54.0%) patients presented with acne
PAPA syndrome manifests as pyogenic sterile arthritis, PG, and cystic acne

checklist.why: Third element of the PAPA triad.

checklist.name: hidradenitis suppurativa

quotes.text: PASH syndrome is distinguished from PAPA syndrome by the presence of HS and the absence of pyogenic arthritis
PAPASH syndrome, which stands for pyogenic arthritis, pyoderma gangrenosum, acne, and suppurative hidradenitis
hidradenitis (n = 2, 3.2%)

checklist.why: Marks the PASH and PAPASH forms of the PSTPIP1 spectrum.

checklist.name: skin or soft-tissue abscesses

quotes.text: abscess (n = 5, 7.9%)
Vaccinations and minor trauma have been reported to induce bruises or abscesses
Recurrent perianal and gluteal abscesses

checklist.why: Recurrent, often sterile abscesses are reported in both PAPA and PAMI.

checklist.name: sterile osteomyelitis or osteolytic bone lesions

quotes.text: osteomyelitis (n = 5, 7.9%)
sterile osteolytic bone lesions
Arthralgia, aseptic osteomyelitis

checklist.why: Bone involvement distinct from arthritis, reported in PAPA and PAMI.

checklist.name: fever

quotes.text: Fever is rarely observed.
fevers were described in 51% of patients (19/37)

checklist.why: More frequent in PAMI than in PAPA; case reports state it either way.

checklist.name: elevated inflammatory markers (CRP, ESR or SAA)

quotes.text: Systemic inflammation was evidenced in all reported cases using the monitoring of CRP, ESR or SAA.
characterized by a persistent severe systemic, joint, and cutaneous inflammation
elevated acute phase reactants (ESR 56 mm/h and CRP 37 mg/L)

checklist.why: Systemic inflammation is a hallmark of PAMI and is measured in PAPA.

checklist.name: anemia

quotes.text: mild to severe anemia in 100%
Hypochromic microcytic anemia (Hb 86g/L)

checklist.why: Present in every reviewed PAMI patient; also seen in PAPA.

checklist.name: neutropenia

quotes.text: neutropenia in 98% of cases
neutropenia persists in all patients

checklist.why: Hallmark of PAMI that distinguishes it from PAPA.

checklist.name: thrombocytopenia

quotes.text: Thrombocytopenia was present in 41% of cases
hepatosplenomegaly, pancytopenia, and failure to thrive

checklist.why: Third cytopenia in PAMI; pancytopenia is recorded through anemia, neutropenia and thrombocytopenia.

checklist.name: splenomegaly

quotes.text: Splenomegaly complicated the presentation of 70% of patients (29/41)
splenomegaly (n = 4, 6.3%)

checklist.why: Common in PAMI and reported in PAPA.

checklist.name: hepatomegaly

quotes.text: hepatomegaly was seen in 56% (23/41)
hepatosplenomegaly, pancytopenia, and failure to thrive

checklist.why: Common PAMI feature, reported separately from splenomegaly.

checklist.name: lymphadenopathy

quotes.text: lymphadenopathy (39%)
lymphoproliferation, anemia, and neutropenia

checklist.why: Part of the lymphoproliferation of PAMI.

checklist.name: growth failure or failure to thrive

quotes.text: Growth failure was reported in 57% (19/33)
experience failure to thrive

checklist.why: Frequent in PAMI, the early-onset severe form.

checklist.name: hyperzincemia

quotes.text: Markedly elevated concentrations of zinc and MRP8/14 were detected in all tested patients.
the high serum zinc levels specifically in PAMI syndrome

checklist.why: Laboratory hallmark that distinguishes PAMI from other PSTPIP1 disease.

checklist.name: hypercalprotectinemia (elevated MRP8/14)

quotes.text: A hallmark of the disease are the increased serum levels of myeloid-related protein (MRP) 8/14 (S100A8/A9 or calprotectin) and zinc
also referred to as hyperzincaemia and hypercalprotectinaemia

checklist.why: Laboratory hallmark that distinguishes PAMI from other PSTPIP1 disease.

checklist.name: inflammatory bowel disease or colitis

quotes.text: inflammatory bowel disease (n = 4, 6.3%)
16% of cases experiencing flare-ups of colitis and/or chronic diarrhea
Inflammatory colitis has been associated with PAPASH syndrome in two reported cases.

checklist.why: Gastrointestinal involvement named in all three sources.

checklist.name: kidney involvement (proteinuria, hematuria or nephropathy)

quotes.text: proteinuria (n = 5, 7.9%)
heterogenous nephropathies can be part of the clinical spectrum of the syndrome
the incidence of hematuria and proteinuria in patient 1 was consistent with the literature

checklist.why: Renal involvement reported in PAPA and in 13% of PAMI.

checklist.name: recurrent infections

quotes.text: 16 (37%) out of 43 patients were reported to have experienced recurrent infections

checklist.why: Reported in over a third of PAMI patients.

left_out: pathergy: reported in 5/63 PAPA patients (34745107) and for PASH (38031879); left out for space, and less often stated than abscesses, which both PAPA and PAMI sources name
pustular rash, erythema, skin ulcer, psoriasis, rosacea (34745107, each <10%): rare, and skin ulcer overlaps pyoderma gangrenosum
joint destruction or deformity (34745107, 17.5%): a complication of arthritis close to an outcome
elevated serum IL-18 and IL-1beta (38031879, 37628706): measured in few patients; distinguishes mutation carriers rather than a clinical feature reported per patient
pancytopenia and hepatosplenomegaly as items: covered by anemia, neutropenia, thrombocytopenia, splenomegaly and hepatomegaly (no overlap rule)
macrophage activation syndrome (37628706, 4/43): rare; 38031879 says IL-18 elevation in PAPA does not raise MAS risk
developmental delay (11%) and hemorrhagic diathesis (11%) in PAMI (37628706): less frequent than the items kept
otitis (34745107, 3/63): an infection, would sit inside recurrent infections
uveitis (1/63), keratitis and oral ulcer (single patients), thrombosis, AML, T-LGL proliferation, antiphospholipid syndrome (34745107): single or very rare reports
autoantibodies (antineutrophil antibodies, ANA, RF), NK cell deficiency, bone marrow dysplasia (37628706): tested in subsets only
dysregulated neutrophils / NET formation, PSTPIP1 hyperphosphorylation, pyrin binding (38031879): mechanism, not patient phenotype
PG and HS lesion morphology (38031879): described for PG and HS in general, narrower than the items kept
age at onset (PAMI median 13 months or 3.9 years, PAPA median 4 years): an onset attribute, not a feature
notes: Sources: 38031879 (Satoh 2024, review of PG, HS and syndromes; only its PAPA/PAMI, PASH and PAPASH sections were used), 37628706 (Mejbri 2023, systematic review of 43 PAMI patients) and 34745107 (Wang 2021, 3 PAPA patients plus a review of 76). PAPA triad and skin items (arthritis, pyoderma gangrenosum, acne, abscesses, osteomyelitis, hidradenitis) come mainly from 34745107 and 38031879; hidradenitis suppurativa marks PASH/PAPASH (38031879; PASH there is genetically heterogeneous, PAPASH is placed in the PAPA spectrum) and appears in 2/63 PAPA patients (34745107). Hematologic, organ and laboratory items (anemia, neutropenia, thrombocytopenia, splenomegaly, hepatomegaly, lymphadenopathy, growth failure, hyperzincemia, hypercalprotectinemia, elevated inflammatory markers, recurrent infections) come mainly from 37628706, with support from 38031879. Fever, colitis/IBD and kidney involvement are named in two or three sources. Some quotes come from per-patient tables (37628706 Table 1, 34745107 Table 2). Pancytopenia in a paper should be recorded as anemia, neutropenia and thrombocytopenia; hepatosplenomegaly as hepatomegaly and splenomegaly. Started from the first helper's 14-item draft (38031879 only); dropped its 'persistent systemic inflammation' (now elevated inflammatory markers), 'elevated serum IL-18' and 'pathergy' (see left_out), and split its composites.
